territorial_scope.description: Federal statute of the United States; obligations apply to chatbot providers serving covered users, and subsection (h) preempts state laws on the same matters.

evidence.quote: Be it enacted by the Senate and House of Representatives of the United States of America in Congress assembled,

summary.short: Bill requiring chatbot providers to disclose to minor users that chatbots are AI systems, bar chatbots from falsely claiming licensed-professional status, require crisis resources and break reminders, and address harmful content. Enforced by the FTC and state attorneys general; applies one year after enactment.
summary.long: Bill applying to chatbot providers and covered users, meaning users the provider knows, or would know but for willful disregard, are minors under 17. Providers may not give covered users a chatbot that claims to be a licensed professional unless true. They must disclose in plain, age-appropriate language that the chatbot is an artificial intelligence system and not a natural person, at the first interaction and when asked, and must provide suicide and crisis hotline resources when suicide is raised. They must maintain reasonable policies prompting a break after three hours of continuous interaction and addressing sexual material harmful to minors, gambling, and illegal drugs, tobacco and alcohol. Violations are treated as violations of an FTC rule on unfair or deceptive practices; the FTC enforces them, and state attorneys general may sue as parens patriae for injunctions, compliance, damages and other relief. States are preempted from regulating the same matters. Subsections (a) to (c) take effect one year after enactment. HHS, through NIH, must study chatbot effects on minors' mental health over four years and report within four years of enactment.

relations.target_text: Federal Trade Commission Act, including section 18(a)(1)(B) (15 U.S.C. 57a(a)(1)(B)) and 15 U.S.C. 41 et seq.
relations.note: Violations of subsections (a), (b) and (c) are treated as violations of an FTC regulation under section 18(a)(1)(B); the FTC enforces them with the Act's jurisdiction, powers and duties incorporated.

relations.target_text: National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020, section 5002 (15 U.S.C. 9401)
relations.note: The term 'artificial intelligence' in this Act takes the meaning given in that section.

evidence.quote: has the meaning given such term in section 5002 of the National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020 (15 U.S.C. 9401)

relations.target_text: State and political subdivision laws, rules and requirements covering a matter described in Sec. 2(a), (b) or (c)
relations.note: States and their political subdivisions may not prescribe, maintain or enforce such provisions. Sec. 2(f) separately gives state attorneys general and agencies a civil action under this Act.

evidence.quote: No State or political subdivision of a State may prescribe, maintain, or enforce any law, rule, regulation, requirement, standard, or other provision having the force and effect of law

notes: Introduced bill; the document is the introduced text and records no legislative events, so none are coded. Sec. 2(d) delays subsections (a), (b) and (c) to one year after enactment, while the enforcement (e), (f) and preemption (h) provisions refer to them without a start date. The long title reads 'for other proposes' as written. 'Minor' means an individual under 17 (Sec. 2(k)(5)). Sec. 2(g) (HHS/NIH study, report due not later than 4 years after enactment) is a government research duty and is not coded here. Target instrument IDs are null because no registry IDs were supplied. section_status is required by the schema; relation entries are present above.

thresholds.variable_text: minor: individual under the age of 17 years
thresholds.measurement: Age of the individual; the provider's actual knowledge or willful disregard determines whether the user is a covered user (Sec. 2(k)(4))
thresholds.consequence: Individuals under 17 are minors; a minor user whom the provider knows or willfully disregards as such is a covered user entitled to the Act's protections
thresholds.conditions: Provider has actual knowledge that the user is a minor, or would know if not for willful disregard (covered user definition)

evidence.quote: The term “minor” means an individual under the age of 17 years.

thresholds.variable_text: duration of continuous and uninterrupted interaction of a covered user with a chatbot (hours)
thresholds.measurement: Continuous and uninterrupted interaction of the covered user with the chatbot of the provider
thresholds.consequence: Provider must maintain policies ensuring the chatbot advises the covered user to take a break at that point
thresholds.conditions: Applies to covered users; interaction must be continuous and uninterrupted

evidence.quote: a continuous and uninterrupted interaction of the covered user with the chatbot has lasted for 3 hours
